title: An almost-linear bound on planar halving lines
formal: For every ε>0, does a constant C_ε exist such that every even n≥2 and every n-point set P⊂ℝ² with no three collinear determine at most C_ε n^(1+ε) halving lines?
definitions: A halving line is the unique line through two distinct points of P with exactly (n−2)/2 of the remaining points in each open half-plane. Count distinct such lines, equivalently unordered endpoint pairs under the general-position hypothesis. Coordinates may be arbitrary real numbers. C_ε must be independent of n and P. This is an extremal counting question rather than the running time of a line-enumeration algorithm.

context_blocks.text: Halving lines describe the combinatorial complexity of central levels in arrangements and of balanced geometric partitions. Their maximum number remains one of the central gaps in planar discrete geometry.

The almost-linear conjecture asks for n^{1+o(1)}, not a linear or polylogarithmic bound. The Open Problems Project connects the question with the broader k-set problem. Its consequences concern the size of geometric structures that algorithms must represent.

why: Determine a basic geometric complexity bound underlying arrangements, levels and range-search structures.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the specified quantifiers, model and guarantees. A conditional theorem settles only that conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
